sketches.title: Reply-All Riot
sketches.premise: A normal group chat gets one awkward message. Take turns posting what appears next, as the chat lurches from mild trouble toward public disaster. The host announces each new scandal like it is a royal crisis.
sketches.criterion: The Judge accepts one plain chat event caused by the whole visible chat so far; a skipped link, a neat fix or sign-off, an undo or deleted-message escape, or a person and setting the chat could not possibly contain fails.
sketches.move_shape: Write one new message, reply, reaction, or chat event beginning with “Then,” and make the problem worse while leaving a fresh detail to trigger next; example: “Then Maya replies, ‘Which Alex?’ and tags all three Alexes.”

sketches.title: Wrong Window
sketches.premise: A group chat is trying to discuss one harmless plan, but messages keep landing in the wrong place. Take turns making the mistake spread through the chat until private jokes, screenshots, and excuses collide. The host treats every ping like a fresh bullet fired into the chandelier.
sketches.criterion: The Judge accepts one next message or chat action that is plainly caused by the latest mistaken audience and still leaves a new audience or secret in play; jumping to a consequence, ending with an apology or silence, deleting or correcting the mistake, or adding someone who could not see the chat fails.
sketches.move_shape: Add one message or reaction that goes to the wrong person or group and creates a new problem; example: “Then Priya sends her roast of Dan to the work chat instead of the friends chat.”

sketches.title: Mod Summons
sketches.premise: A group chat has a harmless argument, and every attempt to keep order creates a louder mess. Take turns adding the next message, rule, vote, or roast as the chat invents its own ridiculous court. The host serves each ruling with velvet pomp and a knife behind the smile.
sketches.criterion: The Judge accepts one chat event that follows from the current argument or rule and changes who has power, what is allowed, or what evidence matters; a jump to a verdict, a final peace, an undo of a ruling, or a witness who has no way to know the facts fails.
sketches.move_shape: Post one new court-style message that responds to the standing dispute and creates the next issue; example: “Then Leo declares himself judge and bans the word ‘technically,’ which is the word everyone needs.”

sketches.title: Seen-Zone Panic
sketches.premise: Someone in a group chat asks a simple question and gets left on read. Take turns showing the next message, reaction, rumor, or real-world interruption as the silence becomes impossible to ignore. The host narrates each blue tick as a tiny bell tolling for friendship.
sketches.criterion: The Judge accepts one event caused by the unanswered message, the visible read status, or the group’s guesses, and it must create a new reason for someone to react; jumping to the hidden truth, ending when the answer arrives, retracting a message, or using knowledge no chat member could have gained fails.
sketches.move_shape: Add one message or chat action that responds to the silence without resolving it; example: “Then Nia posts, ‘Cool, I’ll assume that means yes,’ and books the table.”

sketches.title: Screenshot Season
sketches.premise: A group chat contains one risky joke, and someone saves proof of it. Take turns adding the next message, screenshot, caption, or accusation as the proof travels farther than anyone expected. The host presents every crop and blur as evidence in the trial of a very stupid empire.
sketches.criterion: The Judge accepts one new piece of chat evidence or one reaction directly caused by the latest shared proof, while leaving a fresh question about who saw or changed it; skipping how it spread, stopping with a confession or deletion, undoing the screenshot, or inventing a viewer outside the possible chain fails.
sketches.move_shape: Add one screenshot-related event that follows from the last proof and makes its reach or meaning worse; example: “Then Sam screenshots the screenshot, but the crop still shows the original sender’s name.”

sketches.title: Bot With Teeth
sketches.premise: A group chat adds a helpful bot for polls, reminders, or chores, and the bot starts taking every message painfully seriously. Take turns giving the bot one next action or the group’s response, letting its rules turn small jokes into large problems. The host explains each automated blunder as the proud birth of a new machine god.
sketches.criterion: The Judge accepts one action or reply caused by the bot’s latest rule, command, or misunderstanding and leaves a new instruction, target, or conflict; jumping to a full takeover, ending by shutting the bot off, undoing a command, or making the bot know something never posted fails.
sketches.move_shape: Add one bot message or one human reply that follows from the last posted command and creates a sharper rule or target; example: “Then the bot sees ‘kill the meeting’ and schedules a three-hour meeting called KILL.”
